newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end sharply lower.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures extended early losses to end sharply lower after heavy trade on Tuesday as long-liquidation and some stop-loss selling gathered force amid views that spot gold may dip further, traders said.
Comments by Japanese government officials expressing concern over the recent rapid fall of the yen against the dollar also encouraged heavy selling on TOCOM, they said.
Gold prices ranged from 25 yen to 29 yen per gram lower, with benchmark December ending down 28 yen at 1,315 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $357.60/8.10 per ounce at 0712 GMT, against $357.50/358.00 in New York on Monday.

In the bullion market, early buying by Japanese trade houses in arbitrage trade with TOCOM helped spot prices stabilise after heavy losses overnight, but the trade houses switched to two-way trade later in the session.

"Sentiment remains gloomy. December gold could probe last year's low of 1,303 yen, while spot gold remains vulnerable to steep losses with no bullish factors in sight," one trader said. He pegged initial support for bullion at $354 to $355.
The firm U.S. stock market, combined with fears of central bank gold sales and weak physical demand, fueled bearish sentiment in the gold market, traders said.
World gold prices have fallen sharply since the start of the year, hitting their lowest levels in more than three years.
TOCOM silver and platinum futures also settled lower, following gold, but palladium's performance was mixed.
Benchmark December silver ended 2.3 yen per 10 grams lower at 176.4 yen. Benchmark December platinum ended 21 yen weaker at 1,334 yen.
Palladium was mixed with nearbys firmer and deferred months weaker. Benchmark December palladium settled five yen per gram lower at 433 yen.
